calls.head: Don’t buy Oettinger’s record against the Sabres
calls.body: Oettinger has been a wall against the Sabres since 2023-24, well above his usual. But three seasons of data say a goalie’s record against one team tells us nothing about the next meeting, so don’t be surprised if Oettinger isn’t that wall tonight.
calls.call: If Oettinger starts, his save percentage lands closer to his usual .903 than to his .937 against the Sabres.

calls.title: Oettinger had the Sabres’ number again
calls.plain: Oettinger’s night looked more like his record against the Sabres than his usual. Three seasons of evidence say it’s still a coincidence.

calls.head: The Stars’ edge in the penalty kill
calls.body: The Stars are one of the league’s best for the penalty kill, and the Sabres are around the middle. It’s the widest gap between these two, though not a huge one.
calls.call: The Stars’ penalty kill allows less per 60 than the Sabres’.

surprises.head: Jake Oettinger stole one with a shutout
surprises.body: Oettinger stopped all 22 shots, worth 2.6 expected goals. That is more than Dallas’s winning margin. Starting goalies have a night this good about once every 30 starts.

story.head: Oettinger shuts out the Sabres
paras: Jamie Benn struck first for the Stars late in the second, his 1,000th NHL point, and Wyatt Johnston added insurance on the power play with 42 seconds left.

The Stars had the better of the chances, outshooting the Sabres 30-22 (24-11 at 5-on-5). Jake Oettinger, who gave up six goals against Winnipeg in his last start, stopped all 22 shots for the Stars, and Alex Lyon kept the Sabres in it, stopping 28 of 30.
Jiří Kulich took three penalties on his own. The Stars killed all five Sabres power plays. The Stars moved to 11-6-2, fourth in the Central, while the Sabres fell to 8-8-4, sixth in the Atlantic.

items.text: The Sabres are winless in four (0-3-1).

The Stars won without Miro Heiskanen, Oskar Bäck, Lian Bichsel and others. Taking into account how much value each of these missing players usually adds, only the Avalanche and the Mammoth were missing more at the time.
Kyle Burroughs made his Stars debut.
Zach Metsa was in NHL.com’s projected lineup, but Louis Crevier played instead.
